articles.title: Building Scalable APIs with Laravel
articles.abstract: A practical guide to designing high-throughput RESTful APIs: strict FormRequests, idempotent endpoints, rate limiting, and contract testing with OpenAPI.

sections.heading: 1. The Architectural Role of the API Gateway
sections.content: When designing APIs intended to serve multiple clients—mobile apps, web frontends, and external webhooks—the API layer must act as a strict gatekeeper. It is responsible for payload normalization, rate enforcement, token authentication, and contract compliance before business services ever receive input.

sections.heading: 2. Idempotency Keys and Atomic Locks
sections.content: To prevent duplicate execution during client network retry storms, incoming mutate requests carry an Idempotency-Key. Redis stores the hashed request with a 24-hour TTL. If the key exists, the cached result is returned immediately with a 200 OK without re-executing state mutation.

sections.heading: 3. Eloquent Resource Transforms & OpenAPI Synchronization
sections.content: Controllers should never return Eloquent models directly. By passing models through JsonResource transformers and annotating them with L5-Swagger attributes, your OpenAPI documentation remains in sync with actual wire payloads.

articles.title: My Development Workflow in 2026
articles.abstract: Tools, habits, and mindset for building robust backend systems: Docker environments, Laravel Pulse profiling, PHPStan level 8, and automated CI/CD checks.

sections.heading: 1. Local Consistency via Containerization
sections.content: Every service runs in containerized Docker setups with matching PHP 8.3, MySQL 8, and Redis configurations. This eliminates the "works on my machine" anti-pattern and guarantees reproducible builds across dev, staging, and production.

sections.heading: 2. Static Analysis: PHPStan & Larastan at Level 8
sections.content: Writing PHP without static analysis is like walking on a wire without a net. By running Larastan at Level 8 in CI pipelines, null pointer exceptions, incorrect return types, and invalid docblocks are caught before code review.

sections.heading: 3. Real-Time Telemetry with Laravel Pulse & Horizon
sections.content: Profiling slow queries and queue worker throughput in real time allows pinpointing N+1 queries and memory bloat during active development cycles.

articles.title: What I've Learned as a Developer
articles.abstract: Key lessons, mistakes, and architectural principles that transformed my journey from writing syntax to engineering reliable, scalable backend systems.

sections.heading: 1. Simplicity Outlives Cleverness
sections.content: Early in my engineering journey, I favored clever one-liners and complex abstractions. Over time, maintaining high-traffic production platforms taught me that explicit, readable code with clear transactional boundaries is far superior to esoteric designs.

sections.heading: 2. Databases Are the Ultimate Bottleneck
sections.content: Code is easy to scale horizontally with stateless containers. Databases are stateful and bounded by disk I/O, lock contention, and index structures. Investing time in schema design, composite indexing, and query execution plans pays the highest dividends.

sections.heading: 3. Fail Fast, Log Contextually
sections.content: When something fails in a background worker, vague error logs are useless. Structured JSON logging with correlation IDs, job payload contexts, and stack traces allows resolving production issues in minutes rather than hours.

articles.title: SQL Query Optimization: From Slow Scans to Index-Only Executions
articles.abstract: A practical deep-dive into examining Postgres/MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE trees, eliminating accidental sequential scans, and leveraging composite covering indexes for high-throughput queries.

sections.heading: 1. The Anatomy of an Unintended Table Scan
sections.content: When relational tables grow past hundreds of thousands of rows, queries that performed well in local development suddenly trigger full table scans. The most common culprit is filtering on multiple columns where only a single-column index exists, or applying SQL functions directly to indexed columns, which prevents the query planner from using the index tree efficiently.
sections.codeSnippet:
-- Problematic Query: Triggers Full Table Scan due to DATE() function
SELECT id, status, total_amount 
FROM orders 
WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2026-04-12' AND status = 'completed';

-- Optimized Query: Range scan utilizing composite index (status, created_at)
SELECT id, status, total_amount 
FROM orders 
WHERE status = 'completed'
  AND created_at >= '2026-04-12 00:00:00' 
  AND created_at <= '2026-04-12 23:59:59';

sections.heading: 2. Understanding Index Left-Prefix Matching
sections.content: A composite B-Tree index on (tenant_id, status, created_at) can be visualized as an index sorted primarily by tenant_id, then by status, then by created_at. Queries filtering by tenant_id alone or (tenant_id, status) utilize the index effectively. However, querying by status alone cannot jump into the index tree and falls back to a scan.

sections.heading: 3. Covering Indexes: Eliminating Heap Table Access
sections.content: When all columns requested in the SELECT clause and WHERE clauses are present within the index leaf pages, the database engine executes an "Index-Only Scan". The engine never visits the actual heap table on disk, resulting in pure in-memory index traversal and sub-millisecond execution times.

articles.title: Reliable Background Jobs: Queues, Retries, and Idempotency
articles.abstract: Designing background queue pipelines that never drop messages, prevent double execution during worker crashes, and handle poisoned tasks gracefully.

sections.heading: 1. The Fallacy of At-Most-Once Processing
sections.content: Network dropouts, worker memory exhaustion, and external API timeouts make guaranteed single execution mathematically impossible. Production queue architectures must be built around "At-Least-Once Delivery" coupled with strict application-level idempotency.

sections.heading: 2. Exponential Backoff with Random Jitter
sections.content: When an external service experiences an outage, retrying immediately causes a "thundering herd" effect that keeps the downstream service overwhelmed. Applying exponential backoff with randomized jitter spreads out incoming retries across an expanding time window.

sections.heading: 3. Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) and Poison Pill Triage
sections.content: Tasks that fail repeatedly past maximum retry thresholds must not block the queue. They are automatically evacuated to a Dead-Letter Queue with full failure context, allowing engineers to inspect the offending payload without losing customer data.

articles.title: Clean Architecture in Laravel: Service Layers & Domain Separation
articles.abstract: Breaking out of fat controllers and bloated Eloquent models: applying Service-Oriented MVC, DTOs, and interface contracts in modern Laravel applications.

sections.heading: 1. Fat Controllers: The Technical Debt Flywheel
sections.content: As projects grow, placing business logic directly inside HTTP controllers leads to unmaintainable code that cannot be re-used by queue workers or CLI commands. A Clean Architecture enforces that controllers only handle HTTP requests and responses, delegating all domain logic to dedicated Service classes.

sections.heading: 2. Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) for Strict Typings
sections.content: Instead of passing raw array payloads between layers, type-safe Data Transfer Objects enforce validation constraints at runtime and provide IDE autocompletion across the entire application stack.

articles.title: Designing Scalable Systems: From Monolith to Decoupled Services
articles.abstract: Strategic patterns for scaling backend systems: caching layers, database read/write replicas, asynchronous decoupling, and fault isolation boundaries.

sections.heading: 1. Modular Monolith Before Microservices
sections.content: Premature microservice extraction introduces distributed latency, network partition failures, and complex distributed transactions. Starting with a cleanly decoupled modular monolith allows moving fast while maintaining strict domain boundaries.

sections.heading: 2. Caching Hierarchy: In-Memory, Redis, and CDN
sections.content: A multi-tier caching strategy guarantees that hot paths never touch the primary transactional database, preserving I/O budget for critical business writes.
